8 Things You Need to Know about Surveillance
8 important truths about surveillance
ai-in-society
Author
Rachel Thomas

Published
August 7, 2019

Over 225 police departments have partnered with Amazon to have access to Amazon’s video footage obtained as part of the “smart” doorbell product Ring, and in many cases these partnerships are heavily subsidized with taxpayer money. Police departments are allowing Amazon to stream 911 call information directly in real-time, and Amazon requires police departments to read pre-approved scripts when talking about the program. If a homeowner doesn’t want to share data from their video camera doorbell with police, an officer for the Fresno County Sheriff’s Office said they can just go directly to Amazon to obtain it. This creation of an extensive surveillance network, the murky private-public partnership surrounding it, and a lack of any sort of regulations or oversight is frightening. And this is just one of many examples related to surveillance technology that have recently come to light.

I frequently talk with people who are not that concerned about surveillance, or who feel that the positives outweigh the risks. Here, I want to share some important truths about surveillance:

Surveillance can facilitate human rights abuses and even genocide
Data is often used for different purposes than why it was collected
Data often contains errors
Surveillance typically operates with no accountability
Surveillance changes our behavior
Surveillance disproportionately impacts the marginalized
Data privacy is a public good
We don’t have to accept invasive surveillance
While I was writing this post, a number of investigative articles came out with disturbing new developments related to surveillance. I decided that rather than attempt to include everything in one post (which would make it too long and too dense), I would go ahead and share the above facts about surveillance, as they are just a relevant as ever.

Surveillance can facilitate human rights abuses and even genocide
There is a long history of data about sensitive attributes being misused, including the use of the 1940 USA Census to intern Japanese Americans, a system of identity cards introduced by the Belgian colonial government that were later used during the 1994 Rwandan genocide (in which nearly a million people were murdered), and the role of IBM in helping Nazi Germany use punchcard computers to identify and track the mass killing of millions of Jewish people. More recently, the mass internment of over one million people who are part of an ethnic minority in Western China was facilitated through the use of a surveillance network of cameras, biometric data (including images of people’s faces, audio of their voices, and blood samples), and phone monitoring.

Adolf Hitler meeting with IBM CEO Tom Watson Sr. in 1937. Source: Computer History
Pictured above is Adolf Hitler (far left) meeting with IBM CEO Tom Watson Sr. (2nd from left), shortly before Hitler awarded Watson a special “Service to the Reich” medal in 1937 (for a timeline of the Holocaust, see here). Watson returned the medal in 1940, although IBM continued to do business with the Nazis. IBM technology helped the Nazis conduct detailed censuses in countries they occupied, to thoroughly identify anyone of Jewish descent. Nazi concentration camps used IBM’s punchcard machines to tabulate prisoners, recording whether they were Jewish, gay, or Gypsies, and whether they died of “natural causes,” execution, suicide, or via “special treatment” in gas chambers. It is not the case that IBM sold the machines and then was done with it. Rather, IBM and its subsidiaries provided regular training and maintenance on-site at the concentration camps: printing off cards, configuring machines, and repairing them as they broke frequently.

Data is often used for different purposes than why it was collected
In the above examples, the data collection began before genocide was committed. IBM began selling to Nazi Germany well before the Holocaust (although continued for far too long), including helping with Germany’s 1933 census conducted by Adolf Hitler, which was effective at identifying far more Jewish people than had previously been recognized in Germany.

It is important to recognize how data and images gathered through surveillance can be weaponized later. Columbia professor Tim Wu wrote that “One [hard truth] is that data and surveillance networks created for one purpose can and will be used for others. You must assume that any personal data that Facebook or Android keeps are data that governments around the world will try to get or that thieves will try to steal.”

Plenty of data collection is not involved with such extreme abuse as genocide; however, in a time of global resurgence of white supremacist, ethno-nationalist, and authoritarian movements, it would be deeply irresponsible to not consider how data & surveillance can and will be weaponized against already vulnerable groups.

Data often has errors (and no mechanism for correcting them)
A database of suspected gang members maintained by California law enforcement officials was found to be full of errors, including 42 babies who had been added to the database when they were less than 1 year old (28 of whom were marked as “admitting to being gang members”). Even worse, there was no process in place for correcting mistakes or removing people once they’ve been added.

An NPR reporter recounts his experience of trying to rent an apartment and discovering that TransUnion, one of the 3 major credit bureaus, incorrectly reported him as having two felony firearms convictions. TransUnion only removed the mistakes after a dozen phone calls and notification that the story would be reported on. This is not an unusual story: the FTC’s large-scale study of credit reports in 2012 found 26% of consumers had at least one mistake in their files and 5% had errors that could be devastating. An even more opaque, unregulated “4th bureau” exists: a collection of companies buying and selling personal information about people on the margins of the banking system (such as immigrants, students, and people with low incomes), with no standards on what types of data are included, no way to opt out, and no system for identifying or correcting mistakes.

Surveillance typically operates with no accountability
What makes the examples in the previous section disturbing is not just that errors occurred, but that there was no way to identify or correct them, and no accountability for those profiting off the error-laden data. Often, even the existence of the systems being used is not publicly known (much less details of how these systems work), unless discovered by journalists or revealed by whistleblowers. The Detroit Police Dept used facial recognition technology for nearly two years without public input and in violation of a requirement that a policy be approved by the city’s Board of Police Commissioners, until a study from Georgetown Law’s Center for Privacy & Technology drew attention to the issue. Palantir, the defense startup founded by billionaire Peter Thiel, ran a program with New Orleans Police Department for 6 years which city council members did not even know about, much less have any oversight.

After two studies found that Amazon’s facial recognition software produced inaccurate and racially biased results, Amazon countered that the researchers should have changed the default parameters. However, it turned out that Amazon was not instructing police departments that use its software to do this either. Surveillance programs are operating with few regulations, no oversight, no accountability around accuracy or mistakes, and in many cases, no public knowledge of what is going on.

Surveillance changes our behavior
Hundreds of thousands of people in Hong Kong are protesting an unpopular new bill which would allow extradition to China. Typically, Hong Kong locals use their rechargeable smart cards to ride the subway. However, during the protests, long lines of people waited to use cash to buy paper tickets (usually something that only tourists do) concerned that they would be tracked for having attended the protests. Would fewer people protest if this was not an option?

In the United States, in 2015 the Baltimore Police Department used facial recognition technology to surveil people protesting the death of Freddie Grey, a young Black man who was killed in police custody, and arrested protesters with outstanding warrants. Mass surveillance could have a chilling impact on our rights to move about freely, to express ourselves, and to protest. “We act differently when we know we are ‘on the record.’ Mass privacy is the freedom to act without being watched and thus in a sense, to be who we really are,” Columbia professor Tim Wu wrote in the New York Times.

Flyer from the company Geofeedia Source
Surveillance disproportionately impacts those who are already marginalized
Surveillance is applied unevenly, causing the greatest harm to people who are already marginalized, including immigrants, people of color, and people living in poverty. These groups are more heavily policed and surveilled. The Perpetual Line-Up from the Georgetown Law Center on Privacy and Technology studied the unregulated use of facial recognition by police, with half of all Americans appearing in law enforcement databases, and the risks of errors, racial bias, misuses, and threats to civil liberties. The researchers pointed out that African Americans are more likely to appear in these databases (many of which are drawn from mug shots) since they are disproportionately likely to be stopped, interrogated, or arrested. For another example, consider the contrast between how easily people over 65 can apply for Medicare benefits by filling out an online form, with the invasive personal questions asked of a low-income mother on Medicaid about her lovers, hygiene, parental shortcomings, and personal habits.

In an article titled Trading privacy for survival is another tax on the poor, Ciara Byrne wrote, “Current public benefits programs ask applicants extremely detailed and personal questions and sometimes mandate home visits, drug tests, fingerprinting, and collection of biometric information… Employers of low-income workers listen to phone calls, conduct drug tests, monitor closed-circuit television, and require psychometric tests as conditions of employment. Prisoners in some states have to consent to be voiceprinted in order to make phone calls.”

Data privacy is a public good, like air quality or safe drinking water
Data is more revealing in aggregate. It can be nearly impossible to know what your individual data could reveal when combined with the data of others or with data from other sources, or when machine learning inference is performed on it. For instance, as Zeynep Tufekci wrote in the New York Times, individual Strava users could not have predicted how in aggregate their data could be used to identify the locations of US military bases. “Data privacy is not like a consumer good, where you click ‘I accept’ and all is well. Data privacy is more like air quality or safe drinking water, a public good that cannot be effectively regulated by trusting in the wisdom of millions of individual choices. A more collective response is needed.”

Unfortunately, this also means that you can’t fully safeguard your privacy on your own. You may choose not to purchase Amazon’s ring doorbell, yet you can still show up in the video footage collected by others. You might strengthen your online privacy practices, yet conclusions will still be inferred about you based on the behavior of others. As Professor Tufekci wrote, we need a collective response.

We don’t have to accept invasive surveillance
Many people are uncomfortable with surveillance, but feel like they have no say in the matter. While the threats surveillance poses are large, it is not too late to act. We are seeing success: in response to community organizing and an audit, Los Angeles Police Department scrapped a controversial program to predict who is most likely to commit violent crimes. Citizens, researchers, and activists in Detroit have been effective at drawing attention to the Detroit Police Department’s unregulated use of facial recognition and a bill calling for a 5-year moratorium has been introduced to the state legislature. Local governments in San Francisco, Oakland, and Somerville have banned the use of facial recognition by police.

Tencent just released Youtu-Parsing-Omni, a compact 5B AI model that can turn almost any type of content into structured JSON.

Documents, images, charts, diagrams, audio, and video, all processed by a single transformer.

What it can do:

▪️ Documents: Extract text, tables, formulas, layouts, and reading order
▪️ Images: Understand charts, flowcharts, and geometric shapes
▪️ Audio: Transcribe speech, identify speakers, and recognize acoustic events
▪️ Video: Analyze frames, extract text and speech, and generate structured reports
▪️ Specialized content: Recognize chemical structures (ChemOCR) and musical notation (PDMX)
Everything is converted into a unified JSON format covering seven task families.
And the benchmarks look impressive:
▪️ 96.96 on OmniDocBench v1.6, reported as SOTA
▪️ 75.08 on OmniParsingBench, the highest reported open-source score, behind Gemini 3 Pro overall
▪️ Just 5B parameters
▪️ vLLM plugin for efficient inference and deployment
The interesting part is having one relatively small model handle tasks that previously required several specialized systems.

Potentially very useful for AI agents, document automation, data extraction, and multimodal search.

My inability to obtain satisfactory resolution of cybersecurity incidents I attributed to the U.S. Department of State and Meta in 2020, compounded by concerns surrounding FBI threat-messaging narratives amplified through News Corp media outlets during 2020–2021, directly influenced my decision to abandon the consumer cybersecurity and venture capital markets.

The four categories I identified—foreign state-sponsored hackers, terrorism, child exploitation, and phishing or financial fraud—contributed to what I perceived as an increasingly adverse reputational and institutional environment for individuals raising cybersecurity concerns.

Although I had developed Metaseeker's consumer privacy portfolio and recognized its potential venture capital appeal, I concluded that continued participation in the sector would expose me to institutional relationships and professional dynamics from which I sought independence.

Consequently, in late 2022 and throughout 2023, I redirected my entrepreneurial resources toward Skipyo's proposed hedge fund and public equity investment strategies, prioritizing financial autonomy over Metaseeker's potential commercial upside. In retrospect, this represented a material opportunity-cost decision: my assessment of institutional risk took precedence over product-market validation and venture scalability.

In retrospect, my decision to prioritize Skipyo's hedge fund strategy over Metaseeker may have constituted a significant capital allocation miscalculation. Metaseeker offered exposure to an expanding cybersecurity and consumer privacy market, with potential for scalable software economics, venture financing, and relatively capital-efficient product validation.

Skipyo, conversely, required institutional limited-partner commitments, credible investment performance, regulatory infrastructure, and substantial assets under management before achieving comparable economic viability. By seeking independence from the cybersecurity and venture capital ecosystems, I effectively exchanged a potentially scalable product opportunity for a financial services model characterized by higher institutional entry barriers and greater dependence on external capital allocation decisions.

Although the decision reflected my assessment of unresolved cybersecurity concerns and the importance of professional autonomy, the economic trade-off was unfavorable if Metaseeker could have demonstrated sustainable customer acquisition and product-market fit. The central entrepreneurial lesson is that institutional disengagement should be weighed against addressable market opportunity, capital efficiency, execution control, and the preservation of strategic optionality.

Also in retrospect, Accenture's alleged cybersecurity red-teaming posture in 2022 could have provided a potential pathway for positioning Metaseeker within Silicon Valley's venture capital ecosystem, leveraging my consulting experience, proximity to technology investors, and growing market demand for consumer privacy solutions.

However, my unresolved concerns regarding the 2020 cybersecurity incidents I attributed to the State Department and Meta, compounded by what I perceived as the FBI's 2020–2021 threat-messaging posture amplified through News Corp media properties, materially influenced my unwillingness to pursue that opportunity.

I regarded the associated narratives concerning foreign hackers, terrorism, child exploitation, and financial cybercrime as creating reputational and institutional risks incompatible with my entrepreneurial objectives.

Consequently, rather than capitalize on a potentially favorable environment for Metaseeker's development and venture financing, I elected to disengage from the cybersecurity and technology investment ecosystems and prioritize Skipyo's hedge fund strategy.

The resulting opportunity cost was the decision to forgo potential venture-backed commercialization in favor of institutional independence, despite Skipyo's substantially higher limited-partner fundraising and market-entry barriers. This explains how my perception of the institutional environment shaped the decision; it does not establish that Accenture offered a venture financing pathway specifically routed through their SV VC networks however it does establish that a coordinated FBI–News Corp campaign from 2020/2021 and the messaging that the cyber industry frequently introduced prevented my interest in seeking Metaseeker's commercialization.

My decision to prioritize Skipyo's public equity and proposed hedge fund investment strategy in late 2022, rather than continue commercializing Metaseeker, created an unexpected pathway into corporate governance innovation. Through Skipyo's investment activities, I established equity positions in four publicly traded companies at levels I understood to satisfy applicable shareholder proposal eligibility thresholds, creating opportunities to examine shareholder rights, board accountability, corporate disclosures, and investor participation mechanisms.

In 2022, this involvement extended to pursuing Microsoft Board of Directors documentation through legal proceedings in Delaware and Washington State, exposing practical challenges associated with information access, governance transparency, and the exercise of shareholder rights. These experiences revealed what I considered a structural inefficiency in public capital markets: despite widespread equity ownership, shareholders lacked a unified, accessible infrastructure for verified discussion, collective engagement, and informed interaction with corporate issuers.

This observation became the foundation for Zindaca, a Shareholder Governance Platform, conceived to connect verified retail and institutional shareholders, facilitate issuer engagement, and democratize access to governance-related information and education.

By mid-2023, I had translated these experiences into an entrepreneurial proposition and pitched Zindaca to Y Combinator, marking a return to technology entrepreneurship through financial market infrastructure rather than consumer cybersecurity or LPA-side Fund Management to evaluate FinTech Startup options.

The strategic irony was that Skipyo's institutional financing challenges ultimately helped generate a potentially venture-scalable governance technology concept in an adjacent sector after an initial decision to move away from Silicon Valley venture capital created the firsthand market insight underlying Zindaca's formation. The broader lesson is that direct participation in complex institutional markets can reveal infrastructure gaps capable of supporting new technology ventures, even when the original investment strategy encounters barriers to scale.

Between 2020 and 2022, I experienced what I understood to be cybersecurity breaches involving Twitter, alongside unresolved concerns regarding other technology platforms. Having subsequently developed investment experience in Twitter through Skipyo's public equity activities, I was preparing to approach Jack Dorsey's former Twitter leadership and cybersecurity personnel to pursue a discreet, technically grounded review of the reported incidents.

My objective was to establish whether historical security records, internal technical expertise, and relevant personnel could substantiate the incidents and facilitate a resolution without unnecessary public escalation.

However, Elon Musk's October 2022 acquisition of Twitter fundamentally altered the company's leadership and institutional structure. The subsequent large-scale workforce reductions, including reported departures across security and technical functions, created uncertainty regarding the continuity of personnel and institutional knowledge potentially relevant to reviewing historical incidents. Although those organizational changes did not establish that evidence had been lost or that a resolution was impossible, they materially reduced my confidence in pursuing the original engagement strategy.

The transition also introduced a different institutional environment. I viewed Musk's relationships across defense technology, national security, Texas-based political and commercial networks, and mass media as potentially complicating an already sensitive cybersecurity matter. These concerns were amplified by what I perceived as Accenture's cybersecurity red-teaming posture toward my employment in 2022 and my earlier concerns regarding FBI threat-messaging narratives carried by News Corp outlets during 2020–2021. I was particularly apprehensive about potential overlap between Musk's media relationships and organizations whose coverage I had previously regarded as adverse. These were assessments of institutional and reputational risk rather than established evidence that Musk, Accenture, News Corp, or government actors coordinated against me.

From an entrepreneurial standpoint, the distinction was consequential. My original position in consumer privacy was explicitly non-defense-oriented: Metaseeker sought to create commercial value by helping individuals protect personal information, reduce unwanted surveillance exposure, and exercise greater control over their digital lives. I regarded unauthorized access, intrusive surveillance, and espionage as risks to be mitigated, not capabilities to be commercialized. In my assessment, deeper engagement with defense-connected cybersecurity networks risked diluting that market positioning, introducing conflicts between consumer trust and national security-oriented commercial relationships. Combined with the Twitter ownership transition and my unresolved employment-related concerns, this created what I considered an unfavorable risk-adjusted environment for continuing Metaseeker or pursuing a quiet resolution through Twitter's former leadership.

Consequently, in late 2022 and throughout 2023, I pursued what I considered the most aggressive but potentially liberating strategic alternative: repositioning Skipyo toward a hedge fund and institutional public equities investment model. Rather than depend on Silicon Valley venture financing or the Washington–Arlington national security technology ecosystem, I sought to establish an independent investment management business through prospective CFA- and pension-related institutional relationships, limited-partner commitments, and conventional capital markets infrastructure. Had those financing efforts succeeded, Skipyo could potentially have operated with greater strategic autonomy, following a traditional New York-style investment management model governed by applicable securities laws, SEC requirements, fiduciary responsibilities, and institutional investor agreements. The intended outcome was not exemption from oversight, but independence from technology-sector gatekeepers through a legally structured, commercially disciplined financial enterprise.

The resulting trade-off was substantial. While Skipyo offered a potential pathway toward institutional autonomy, it also imposed significant fundraising, compliance, track-record, and investor-access hurdles that Metaseeker's venture-backed technology model might not have faced to the same degree. In retrospect, the strategic miscalculation was the decision to prioritize independence from perceived institutional exposure before fully validating the commercial potential of the consumer privacy opportunity.

Following Elon Musk's acquisition of Twitter, his frequent media engagement and visibility across politically connected technology, defense, and business networks heightened my perception of reputational and institutional risk. Against the backdrop of unresolved cybersecurity concerns, I filed litigation against X Corp in late 2023 seeking legal remedies for what I alleged were security violations. This introduced an additional strategic complication: X Corp operated a major social media platform, while Zindaca, which I had pitched to Y Combinator in mid-2023, was itself conceived as a shareholder-focused social and governance platform. Given this overlap, I elected to avoid reliance on journalists, political figures, or broader public narratives as mechanisms for resolving the dispute. Instead, I sought to keep the matter within formal legal channels and paused Zindaca's business-to-consumer development to limit perceived reputational exposure, political entanglement, and potential conflicts between litigation and commercialization.

In mid-2024, I conceived https://t.co/k2m32VJERw as a business-to-business synthetic data and data engineering platform, representing a deliberate shift away from consumer-facing social infrastructure. The decision reflected both my dissatisfaction with what I perceived as unnecessarily aggressive professional dynamics within segments of New York's financial sector and my desire to avoid the interpersonal, reputational, and media-related complexities associated with introducing another social media-oriented startup. Unlike Zindaca, whose value proposition depended on shareholder participation, network effects, and public-facing engagement, https://t.co/k2m32VJERw offered a more technically oriented enterprise model centered on data infrastructure, AI development, and institutional customers. The strategic objective was to preserve exposure to venture-scalable technology opportunities while reducing dependence on consumer social dynamics and politically sensitive stakeholder relationships.

Separately, my litigation involving Microsoft did not produce the substantive outcome I sought. Nevertheless, I regarded my pro se federal court proceedings in 2025 as an important development in my efforts to frame alleged cybersecurity harms through tort-law theories rather than relying exclusively on privacy-law claims. From my assessment of the legal proceedings, the Federal Court proceeded to review in detail and then dismiss the case against Microsoft, not questioning the Torts Basis of the case that was filed, instead citing a Precedent Case suggesting the Financial Claim against Microsoft had been above an expected threshold.

By late 2025 and into 2026, I reconsidered the decision to suspend Zindaca and began repositioning it as a shareholder governance infrastructure platform rather than a conventional consumer social network. The strategic rationale was to pursue greater shareholder accessibility, collective participation, information transparency, and institutional accountability through a scalable commercial product. My unresolved concerns involving Microsoft were an important personal motivation for this renewed focus, but Zindaca's broader commercial proposition extended beyond any individual corporate dispute: a verified platform enabling shareholders to engage with issuers, understand governance matters, and exercise their rights more effectively. I consequently deprioritized https://t.co/k2m32VJERw, placing its development on hold while redirecting attention toward Zindaca's product architecture, governance safeguards, and prospective venture financing, seeking greater market access and power relative to Microsoft that I had sued in Federal Court. 

Unsuccessful efforts to establish investment relationships with Texas and Florida pension institutions in 2023 for Skipyo and retaliation to a few cyber breaches in early 2024 after X/Microsoft had established hacking capabilities in the prior years, materially influenced the decision to pursue an alternative customer market outside conventional U.S. institutional capital networks such as inventing Maza Coffee in 2025 for the Taliban Customer Base. 

Maza Coffee protein beverage was therefore selected not simply as a geographic diversification opportunity, but as a deliberate commercial response to the institutional financing and cybersecurity circumstances I had experienced from Pentagon affiliated orgs such as Microsoft so this decision to pursue that market is casually related to those direct circumstances coming from the Defense involved cyber sector. 

The accompanying infographic examines my professional and entrepreneurial trajectory against the structural reallocation of U.S. venture capital toward DefenseTech, frontier AI, and enterprise infrastructure.

字节群10月国庆假期群精华总结（上）
这一篇含 AI 产品 + 投资分析  + 创作与财富方法论
一、个人 Agent ：Muse vs Grok Bot vs dot

9/30 OpenAI 开了发布会宣布用 Dots + Space 杀进个人 Agent 赛道

大家的体验是：
“没有 Meta 的 Muse 那么丝滑简单，也没有 Grok Bot 那么 geek 有趣。”
“dot 在工作场景打不过 Grok Bot，在生活场景打不过 Muse。”

dot 试图切入工作场景，但目前体验仍有不少问题。dot 回答速度慢、操作 button 要等很久，以及所有聊天都在一个对话框里，回查信息比较费事。其中“代理会用 nebula-dns.crt 重新签发证书，所以理论上你的加密信息会被看到。”甚至有人发现，dot 背后的电脑基本处于不可用状态。

目前如果你需要个人 Agent，这是我们给你的建议：
 - Muse 辅助日常生活助理，包括日程安排、Trip 和购物；
 - Grok 处理工作、学习研究，可以创建多个 agents 互动，可云端可本地，还可以调用 Claude 和 Gemini，甚至能在 Tesla 上使用；但生活邮箱和工作邮箱分开

发邮件时，要求 Agent 先写成草稿放进草稿箱，不要直接发送，自己看过之后再发。读取信息、做前面的准备工作可以交给 Agent，但最后拍板、写入，还是自己来

10/7，Meta 又联合 Sierra 宣布 Personal Agent Protocol（PAP）

三个协议：MCP：Agent 调用工具 / 数据，属于垂直连接。A2A：Agent 把任务托付给另一个 Agent，属于水平协作。PAP：个人 Agent 合规地代表用户找商家办事，解决身份和授权问题。

现在的 Agent 还在学人点网页、填表、打客服电话，又慢又容易翻车；企业一边怕被乱爬，一边不知道对面到底是人还是 bot：没有标准之前，这就是混乱。

但也随之出现新机会：做业务 Agent 对接个人 Agent。
不过 Personal Agent 大战已经开启，这是巨头的战场，创业者慎入。

国内大厂也在推进个人 Agent。腾讯的 WorkBuddy 小程序曾被评价为有点开倒车：因为还只是用 TUI 取代传统 GUI，每个应用依然是分开的入口，各聊各的，各自守着自己的数据。。。但后来 ChatGPT 也推出了类似的小程序形态，于是大家调侃：“骂错了，ChatGPT 抄了腾讯这个小程序，马化腾是个内行。” ^ ^

毕竟腾讯的 QClaw 宣布 12 月 24 日停运，AI 时代还是太快了。。。

二、Anthropic 递交招股书：
ARR 超过 OpenAI？先看清楚口径

9/29，Anthropic 递交招股书，披露的数据很夸张：FY25 收入同比增长 1088% 至 45.9 亿美元；算力和基础设施支出增长 190% 至 73.3 亿美元；经营亏损 80.6 亿美元；年末持有现金及短期投资 202.8 亿美元。两个最大的直接客户合计占总收入的 24%

10/8 晚上，“Anthropic ARR 正式 flip OpenAI 了”的消息把市场带崩了。。。
但仔细拆开口径：没有超过，时间和口径都不一样。

Anthropic 的 run-rate revenue，是把过去 28 天的按量付费销售额乘 13，再加上每月订阅收入乘 12。
OpenAI 的 annualized revenue，则只算上个月的订阅收入乘 12，没包含按量付费，也没包含微软等合作方的销售。
而且 Anthropic 的按量付费销售额包含 AWS、微软、Google 的转售，也没有减去云服务商的分成。拿两个口径不同的数字直接比较，再得出 Anthropic 已经超过 OpenAI 的结论，并不成立。

关于订阅经济学，如果按 API 等价值算，Anthropic 订阅的含金量约是 OpenAI 的 5 倍。虽然订阅收入约占 Anthropic 全部收入的 10%，却可能消耗 40% 以上的推理算力。这也解释了为什么 Anthropic 对把 Max 订阅用量吃满的用户格外敏感。

A/ 封号问题这周同样严重。有同一张卡一直给第二个账号付款、反复尝试，导致第一个账号也被封；另一个账号则因为反代被封。。。达里奥我真是祝你身体健康 🌹

另外，Anthropic 发布 Haiku 5.5，100K token 以内价格降至每百万 token 输入 $0.10、输出 $0.50，相比 Haiku 4.5 的 $1 / $5，降价约 90%。

对于 Opus 5.5，应该是上一代基座模型更好的工程化蒸馏版。Dario 说要放慢，但发版比谁都快。

三、存储退潮，电力接棒：
AI 和大宗商品资源是接下来两大主线

国庆期间，群里最明显的感受是：“整个假期只有存储在挨打。”

多头表示“存储就是近期利润太高了，利润率下降的预期覆盖了整体市场增长的预期。”长期逻辑则是：“数据存储的需求接近无限，资本这阶段认不认成长性另说。”还有猜想：“存储的下一波是物理 AI 和世界模型，看这两个 PPT 概念能不能向前推动。”

但如果下次指数上攻存储不共振，就要警惕了。
对美光的判断则是老话重提：“增长如果主要来自涨价，就不可持续；不可持续的业绩对股价毫无帮助，因为股价对应的是后续的自由现金流，不是之前的。”

而这段时间的新主线，是电力和大宗商品。
电力方向此前关注的包括 BE、CEG、VST、VRT；大宗商品则可以关注巴西市场 EWZ，以及铜相关的紫金矿业。毕竟紫金矿业有一半也是 AI（铜）

现实侧也有佐证：目前算力中心电工紧缺，工资持续上涨；美国的土木和电力行业同样不愁没活，到处都在建数据中心。AI 基建的扩张，已经不只是芯片和服务器的问题，而是进一步拉动电力、工程施工和资源品。

四、有人用 AI 对比了美股群 6 月与 9 月底到 10 月初的聊天，得出了一些很有意思的结果

最核心的转变是存储信仰退潮。
六月“存储”的出现频率约是现在的 1.9 倍，“海力士”约 3.2 倍，HBM 更明显，现在只有六月的约 10%。六月的典型对话是：“有人在存储车上吗？”“你应该问有人没在存储车上吗？”“这个群含存率应该有 50%。”

其次是从“下一个能涨什么”变成“我到底应该怎么长期配置”。QQQ 的讨论密度约是六月的 3.2 倍。“梭哈”下降约 48%，“贷款”下降约 55%，但“止损”增加约 63%。

接着，幸存者偏差意识变强了。
现在有人说“小跌小买、大跌大买”，马上会被质疑：“现在回头看 7 月梭哈当然容易，但你 7 月当时真的梭了吗？”

总结：六月：“存储永远缺 → 两倍海力士 → 今晚梭哪个 → 财富自由。”
现在：“存储我吃过亏了 → 还是配点 QQQ → 杠杆别太高 → 这个 Agent 产品怎么实现 → 晚上美股开盘再看。”

果然亏了才会形成自己的投资体系，人们都一样。

六、亲手写代码已经不再是一项有经济价值的事业
这段时间，关于 AI 如何改变程序员工作的讨论非常密集。

到今年底，几乎所有领域、几乎所有程序员、几乎所有公司，都可能面临这种变化。
这不是说创造本身失去了价值，而是亲手敲代码的那段旅程结束了，一份全新的职业正在出现：成为专业的创造者，驾驭智能来创造新产品。

Anthropic 自己的使用报告也表示：在产生代码的任务中，法律、金融、管理、科研等非技术职业用户的成功率已经接近软件工程师。
真正影响结果的，是用户是否理解自己要解决的问题。大公司的病是人多活少，大家为了假的工作量互相争斗。AI 真正该做的，是把注意力和时间还给人。

公司本质上是一连串 loop：从 prompt 驱动 agent，再由 agent 构成 loop；编码 loop 迭代代码库，业务 loop 重塑业务本身。
其最强形态甚至是：“loop 主动给 CEO 发消息：该改商业模式了。”但 loop 只能爬向局部最优：“决定下一座山在哪里的永远是人。”

所以管理者的三条策略是：
1. 让公司 / 工作自动化——Agent Loop。
2. 把自己网络化，加强人感、建立 IP。
3. 拿赚来的钱投资下一代科技公司。

人感更重要了。因为大量的东西都是 AI 做的，只有少量的人加 AI 做的东西才是好的。

AI 创作：花 21 元做一部 AI 短视频，播放 100 万+，收益只有 4 元。单看平台收益，财务上绝对亏本；但播放带来的讲课和商单，远远超过 21 元成本。

所以：“一定要多创作、坚持创作、坚持输出。”

而创作方式本身也会改变。一个很有意思的概念是 Intentware（意件）：LUI（Language User Interface）仍然只是中间产物，未来的 User Interface 将围绕用户意图构造，而不再拘泥于图形、命令行、语言甚至脑电波。
需要什么，就用什么：“内容生产越容易，难以复制的东西就越值钱。”

AI 可以拷贝宫崎骏的风格，但造不出一个新的宫崎骏：
品味做到极致，就是回到纯粹的自我

七、零散。
MongoDB 因 CEO 离职加盟 Meta 的消息暴跌后，有人复盘了此前清仓的逻辑：“AI 时代之前是 co-founder 特供数据库，有了 AI 就没必要了。”

所谓“用户黏性很强”和“每个工程师都讨厌它”，其实是一体两面：MongoDB 最初使用时摩擦低、开发者体验好，但项目做大之后，应用实现已经和它的机制深度绑定，迁移到其他数据库的摩擦会非常高。
过去很多产品最初由 co-founder 亲自开发，为了追求速度、灵活性和面向应用，会倾向选择 MongoDB。但现在做新产品，不再需要 co-founder 自己手写代码。
“虽然 MongoDB 的存量还在、可以继续榨取价值，但增量很危险。”
所以买入原因不成立了，才会卖。

本地算力硬件大涨，本地模型怎么选？
两台 Spark 跑 GLM-5.3-Flash 和 DeepSeek-V4-Flash
跑 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 要用 4 台 Spark
小模型 Qwen3.8-27B 用 4090 就够了，27B 适合用游戏显卡跑，带宽大。如果是 Mac Studio 的话，还是 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 最合适——专门为这种低带宽大内存设计的 MoE 架构

这周大家发现 Opus 5.5 的“一键成片”功能极度在线
什么都没开，就是纯粹的文本聊天，所有工具都是它自己找自己搞，最终呈现视频效果 / 剧本完整性 / 人声匹配度 / 音乐音效配合度，能过各大视频站收益基准线，程度可以说是能在各种正式的电子音乐官方排名里直接打榜

Seedance 对导演来说是非常好的模型。但 Opus，感觉它自己就是最强的导演。
LLM 不需要自己直接生成每一帧视频，而是可以通过代码、软件和各种工具，自己把完整的制作流程串起来

成本做一个 MV 可能也就 10 美元的 token

🚀 BTFS v4.1.0: THE REAL VALUE OF DECENTRALIZED STORAGE IS IN THE INFRASTRUCTURE

Decentralized storage is about more than distributing files across a network. It also requires reliable storage providers, verifiable metadata, resilient connectivity, and mechanisms that keep data available over time.

BTFS continues to develop this infrastructure within the BitTorrent ecosystem, with BTTC providing blockchain connectivity and smart-contract functionality.

The bigger story is how these components can work together to make decentralized storage more practical for developers, businesses, and Web3 applications. 👇

1️⃣ 🏗️ Decentralized Storage Needs More Than Distributed Files

Traditional cloud storage gives users a relatively straightforward experience: upload a file, receive a reference, and retrieve it when needed.

Decentralized storage aims to distribute data across participating infrastructure rather than relying entirely on one centralized provider.

But distributing files is only one part of the challenge.

A practical system also needs to identify where data is stored, coordinate storage providers, manage storage agreements, verify relevant information, and support dependable retrieval.

BTFS is designed to combine distributed storage with blockchain-based components that help coordinate storage operations.

The strategic objective is to move beyond decentralization as a technical concept and toward a system that developers can use to build real applications.

2️⃣ 🔗 On-Chain Metadata Can Make Storage Information More Verifiable

Metadata describes information about a file, such as its name, format, size, or other attributes required by an application.

In decentralized storage, metadata is important because the system needs a way to associate stored content with the information required to manage and retrieve it.

Using blockchain-based records for selected metadata can improve transparency and make certain information independently auditable.

Smart contracts can provide a structured mechanism for recording and accessing this information without relying exclusively on a private database controlled by one operator.

However, on-chain metadata does not mean that the entire file is stored on the blockchain. Large files generally remain in the storage system, while blockchain records can hold selected metadata or references.

This distinction matters because blockchain storage has different cost and scalability characteristics from decentralized file storage.

3️⃣ 🧩 Metadata and File Content Serve Different Purposes

A decentralized storage architecture typically needs to manage at least two related layers.

▪️ Content layer: Stores the actual file data across the storage infrastructure.

▪️ Metadata layer: Holds information used to identify, describe, locate, or manage that content.

Keeping these roles distinct can help systems scale without placing large amounts of raw file data directly on-chain.

Blockchain records can provide a verifiable reference for certain metadata, while the storage network handles the content itself.

Yet metadata integrity alone cannot guarantee that a file remains available. A reference can remain valid even when the underlying content is temporarily inaccessible.

Reliable storage therefore requires both trustworthy records and operational mechanisms that support data availability and retrieval.

4️⃣ 🌐 BTTC Connectivity Is Part of the Operational Foundation

BTFS operates within a broader ecosystem that includes BitTorrent Chain, or BTTC.

Blockchain connectivity enables software to communicate with the network, query relevant contract information, and submit transactions when authorized.

RPC connectivity is one of the mechanisms through which applications communicate with blockchain nodes.

If a storage application cannot reliably reach an RPC endpoint, it may struggle to retrieve contract information or complete blockchain-dependent operations.

Improving connectivity can therefore contribute to a smoother operational experience.

However, better RPC connectivity does not automatically guarantee higher storage performance, faster file downloads, or stronger decentralization. Those outcomes also depend on node availability, network conditions, application design, and storage-provider performance.

5️⃣ ⚙️ Storage Providers Are Essential to the User Experience

Decentralized storage depends on infrastructure operators that make storage resources available to the network.

In BTFS, Storage Providers are a central part of the storage architecture.

Their role goes beyond simply having disk space. A usable storage network needs mechanisms to discover providers, coordinate storage agreements, manage payments, and establish whether the required service is being delivered.

Smart-contract-based coordination can help make selected operational information more transparent and enforce certain rules.

Nevertheless, decentralization does not remove the need for operational accountability.

Users still need to consider provider reliability, redundancy, retrieval performance, and the consequences of providers becoming unavailable.

A decentralized storage network becomes more useful when its infrastructure can be accessed predictably—not merely when more nodes exist.

6️⃣ 🔄 Automatic Renewal Can Reduce Storage Management Friction

One of the changes documented for BTFS v4.1.0 is support for automatic renewal of storage contracts, alongside manual renewal options.

This addresses a practical problem: storage arrangements have a duration, and users may need to extend them to keep their files stored under the intended conditions.

Without a convenient renewal process, users may have to monitor expiration dates and intervene manually.

Automatic renewal can reduce that burden when it is configured correctly and the necessary conditions are met.

The feature does not mean storage is guaranteed indefinitely. Renewal still depends on the applicable contract, payment arrangements, provider availability, and system operation.

The broader lesson is that decentralized infrastructure must make routine maintenance manageable if it is to serve users beyond technically sophisticated communities.

7️⃣ 📤 Proxy Uploads Can Improve Access in Difficult Network Environments

BTFS v4.1.0 also documents a proxy-upload feature that allows a proxy node to forward client file data to designated Storage Providers.

This can be useful in network environments where direct connections are difficult, including certain restricted or NAT-based configurations.

Instead of requiring every client to establish the same direct connection path, proxying can provide an alternative route for upload traffic.

That may improve accessibility for some users and deployment environments.

But proxying introduces its own operational considerations. The proxy must be available, forwarding must work reliably, and the architecture should clearly define what the proxy can observe or control.

A proxy can help with connectivity, but it should not be confused with a guarantee of complete privacy, censorship resistance, or end-to-end availability.

8️⃣ 🛡️ Reliability Requires More Than Blockchain Records

Blockchain can make selected records auditable and resistant to unauthorized modification under the relevant network's security assumptions.

It cannot, by itself, ensure that every file is available whenever a user requests it.

A robust decentralized storage system must address several separate questions:

▪️ Is the metadata accurate and accessible?

▪️ Is the underlying content still available?

▪️ Can the user retrieve the content efficiently?

▪️ Are storage providers operating as expected?

▪️ Can users detect failures and recover when something goes wrong?

▪️ Are sensitive files protected through appropriate encryption and access controls?

These questions illustrate why storage reliability must be measured across the entire system.

On-chain verification is one valuable component, but it is not a substitute for dependable storage operations, security practices, and recovery mechanisms.

9️⃣ 🧑‍💻 Developers Need Predictable Infrastructure

For decentralized storage to support a wider range of applications, developers need more than a protocol specification.

They need reliable interfaces, clear documentation, predictable error handling, accessible tools, and stable ways to interact with storage providers and blockchain services.

A dependable developer experience reduces the effort required to build applications on top of the infrastructure.

Potential use cases include decentralized application assets, public datasets, distributed content delivery, and other workflows that benefit from content-addressable storage.

These are potential application categories, not evidence that every use case is already widely adopted on BTFS.

The important measure is whether developers can integrate the system efficiently and deliver a better experience for end users.

🔟 📊 Infrastructure Progress Should Be Measured Through Real Performance

Software releases are important milestones, but the value of an infrastructure upgrade becomes clearer through operational results.

For BTFS, useful indicators include:

▪️ Successful upload and retrieval rates.

▪️ Median and high-percentile file retrieval times.

▪️ Storage-provider uptime and availability.

▪️ Contract-renewal success rates.

▪️ RPC response times and error rates.

▪️ Upload failures across different network environments.

▪️ Storage utilization and the level of redundancy.

▪️ The number of applications and users relying on the network.

These measurements would help establish whether infrastructure improvements translate into a more dependable storage experience.

Without performance data, it is difficult to quantify how much a release improves reliability or scalability.

The strongest evidence comes from repeatable benchmarks and real-world usage, not the release announcement alone.

1️⃣1️⃣ 💎 What Does This Mean for BTT and the Wider Ecosystem?

BTFS is part of the wider BitTorrent ecosystem, where BTT is associated with the project's token-based storage and service mechanisms.

More useful storage infrastructure could create opportunities for greater participation by users, developers, and storage providers.

However, a software upgrade does not automatically create additional token demand.

The economic impact depends on how storage services are priced, how payments are made, what role BTT plays in those flows, and whether actual usage grows enough to change demand for the token.

It is important to distinguish technical progress from economic outcomes.

A stronger storage protocol can improve the foundation on which an ecosystem operates, but token value depends on additional factors, including utility, token economics, adoption, liquidity, competition, and broader market conditions.

1️⃣2️⃣ 🚀 The Bigger Picture: Building Infrastructure That Developers Can Trust

BTFS's longer-term challenge is not simply to add features. It is to combine distributed storage, reliable provider coordination, blockchain-based metadata, and accessible developer tooling into a system that works consistently.

The documented v4.1.0 changes—automatic contract renewal, proxy uploads, and on-chain Storage Provider discovery—address practical aspects of storage operations.

The wider BTFS architecture also incorporates blockchain-based metadata management and BTTC connectivity.

Together, these components illustrate the different layers required to make decentralized storage usable.

The next important milestones will be evidence of dependable retrieval, successful renewals, resilient connectivity, growing application adoption, and transparent performance.

The Bottom Line 🌐

Decentralized storage becomes valuable when users can store and retrieve data reliably, developers can integrate it without excessive complexity, and the network can coordinate its infrastructure transparently.

Blockchain metadata can improve verifiability. RPC connectivity can support communication with on-chain services. Storage-provider mechanisms, renewal workflows, and proxy uploads can address practical operational challenges.

But none of these features alone guarantees adoption or commercial success.

Infrastructure is the foundation. Reliability earns trust. Real usage is what demonstrates value.

⚠️ This post is for informational purposes only and is not financial advice. Infrastructure upgrades do not guarantee token appreciation or future investment performance.

Agent evaluations are hard to reproduce. This framework gives you a concrete environment.

AgentEnv Framework is a Python SDK and CLI for builders creating agentic environments and tasks that grade agents inside them.

It helps you move from an environment definition to a repeatable agent run by building containerized environments into versioned images, deploying them behind a gateway, and scoring what the agent did.

Key features:

• Environment protocol – containerized servers speak the open agentenv-framework-protocol
• Agent task grading – point an agent at an environment and score what it did
• Versioned images – build environments into versioned images before deployment
• Fast local starting point – run the built-in hello task with no Docker, model, or configuration
• Plugin extension points – installed packages can register environments, task steps, artifacts, providers, and explorer plugins

It’s open-source (Apache License 2.0 license).

AIエージェントが「自分自身」をRustで書き直した。2,209体・2,287億トークン・2週間で、起動は約14倍速、メモリは5分の1以下に

現地時間10/9、Prime Intellectがオープンソースのコーディングエージェント「Prime Agent」をTypeScriptからRustへ全面移植したと発表しました。

ポイントは、移植したのが人間ではなく、Prime Agent自身だということです。2,000体を超えるエージェントの群れを自分で指揮して、自分のコードを丸ごと書き直しました。

Prime AgentはGitHubで2.1万スター超、8月の公開以来30万回以上ダウンロードされ、処理したトークンは8兆を超えるとされています。確認した時点では、このRust移植についての日本語解説はQiita・Zennともにまだ見当たりませんでした。

■結論
・「AIに大規模な書き直しをさせる」は、実験ではなく製品のリリースで使える段階に来た
・効いたのはモデルの賢さより、「正しく移植できたか」を機械で判定する検証の仕組み
・書いた役と採点する役を別のエージェント、別のモデルに分けたのが肝
・ただし速度比較は自社ベンチマークで、最後の仕上げは人間がレビューしている。全自動ではありません

■何が起きたのか
期間はおよそ2週間。Prime Agentが1体の親エージェントとして全体を指揮し、子・孫・ひ孫まで階層的にエージェントを生み出して作業を分担しました。

公開された数字は次の通りです。
・参加したエージェント 2,209体
・エージェント同士のメッセージ 16,758件
・消費トークン 合計2,287億
・使ったサンドボックス 1万個以上
・推論はPrime Inferenceで提供しているGLM-5.3

内訳は、Rustへの移植本体が1,981体・1,930億トークン、移植後の性能チューニングが228体・357億トークンです。

オーケストレーター自体は、8コアのCPUマシン2台で動かしています。1台あたり100体以上の子エージェントを同時に動かし、コンパイルや差分チェックなどの重い処理はサンドボックス側に逃がしたそうです。

■どうやって「勝手に書き直す」を成立させたか
人間が主にやったのは、コードを書くことではなく「移植が正しいか」を判定する仕組みを作ることでした。

用意した判定は4種類です。
・画面の一致：TypeScript版とRust版を同じ台本で動かし、ターミナルに描画される画面を1コマずつ比較
・動作の一致：同じ入力から同じセッション記録、同じモデルへのリクエストが出るかを比較
・通信の一致：内部のプロトコルのメッセージ型がすべて旧版と合っているかを確認
・機能の一致：エージェントが旧版を部品ごとに監査し、「一致・一部・未実装」に分類

そのうえで、1つのタスクを4体のエージェントに順番に通しています。
1. Planner：仕様、旧版の正しい動作、合格条件を決める
2. Implementer：専用の作業ツリーでRustのコードを書く
3. Reviewer：実装役とは別のモデル・別の文脈で、「この変更はどこが間違っているか」を探す
4. Verifier：新しいサンドボックスでビルドし、一致チェックとテストを流す

レビューか検証で落ちれば実装役に差し戻し、両方通ったらマージ。親エージェントはコードを1行も書かず、監視とマージと優先順位の判断だけに徹しました。

「コードを書いたエージェントは、自分のコードの採点が甘くなる」という理由で、書く役と採点する役を分けたと説明されています。

■数字で見る
移植だけでは速くなっていません。ここが面白いところです。

移植直後のRust版は、インストールサイズが旧版の172.1MBから206.7MBに増え、エージェント画面の切り替えも78.0ミリ秒から118.8ミリ秒へ遅くなっていました。

そこから、別の親エージェントが3日間、「一致を壊さずにベンチマークを改善し続けろ」という目標だけで改善ループを回しました。数値目標はあえて置かず、144件以上の実験と監査を記録し、69件以上の改善をマージしています。

TypeScript版と最終的なRust版の比較です。
・起動して入力できるまで（初回）：736.1ミリ秒 → 51.9ミリ秒（約14.2倍速）
・同（2回目以降）：552.3ミリ秒 → 41.4ミリ秒（約13.3倍速）
・大きなセッションを読み込んだ時のメモリ：1,130MB → 237.3MB（約4.8分の1）
・インストールサイズ：172.1MB → 59.6MB（約2.9分の1）
・エージェント画面の切り替え：78.0ミリ秒 → 12.8ミリ秒（約6.1倍速）

他のツールとの比較も出しています。起動から最初の表示まで、Rust版Prime Agentは23.6ミリ秒。同じ条件でClaude Codeは264.6ミリ秒、Codex CLIは296.8ミリ秒、Piは306.3ミリ秒、Hermes Agentは1,715.3ミリ秒でした。起動後のメモリもRust版は106.0MBで、比較対象の中で最も小さい数字です。

改善の中身は大きく3つで、起動と描画の経路から処理を外す、ポーリングをイベント待ちに置き換える、大きなセッションを読み終えたらすぐメモリを解放する、というものでした。

コードの構造も変わっています。9つのクレートに分割し、最大のファイルは約15,000行から約2,500行に。セッションごとに別プロセスで動くので、1つが落ちても他は止まりません。この作り直しのおかげで、Windows対応（ベータ）とHomebrewでのインストールも加わりました。

■なぜ今これが重要か
大規模な書き直しは、これまで「やりたいけど誰も手を付けられない」仕事の代表でした。

今回の事例が示しているのは、AIに書かせる量を増やすことより、「合っているかを機械で判定できる状態」を先に作ることが決定的だという点です。判定があれば、エージェントは自分で進み具合を測り、壊れた変更をマージ前に止められます。

もう一つは、エージェントがコードの大半を書く前提で、言語側の安全装置を重視していることです。Rustを選んだ理由として、型やエラー処理の抜けをコンパイラが止めてくれることを挙げ、「エージェントがコードの大半を書くなら、それが効いてくる」と書いています。

■注意点
・他ツールとの速度比較は、Prime Intellect独自のテスト環境での測定です。共通の基準がないので慎重に見てほしい、と本人たちも書いています
・測っているのは起動や画面の反応で、モデルの推論時間は含みません。体感の作業スピードがそのまま14倍になるわけではありません
・一致チェックで確認できたのは、テストで動かした範囲だけです。範囲外のバグは社内で使ってから見つかり、リリース品質にするまでの数週間は人間がすべての結果をレビューしています
・2,287億トークンという規模は、自前の推論基盤とサンドボックスを持つ会社だからできた数字です。同じことを外部のAPIでやれば、相当な費用になります
・GLM-5.3は同社の推論サービスで提供しているモデルです。自社の推論基盤とサンドボックスの宣伝も兼ねた発表だと理解して読むのが妥当です

■次のアクション
1. 自分のプロジェクトで「移植や大きなリファクタリングをしたいが手が出ない部分」を1つ選ぶ
2. いきなり書かせず、先に旧版と新版を同じ入力で動かして出力を比べるテストを作る
3. 書く役とレビューする役を、別のモデル・別のセッションに分ける
4. 性能改善は、数値目標を決めずに「ベンチマークを壊さず良くし続ける」ループとして回してみる

Prime Agent本体を試すなら、公式のワンライナーで入ります。今回のリリースでWindowsとHomebrewにも対応しました。

GitHub
PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent

■OpenClawで使うなら
OpenClaw系でエージェントを回している人にとって、そのまま持ち帰れるのは「役割の分け方」です。

・1つのスキルに全部やらせず、計画、実装、レビュー、検証を別のサブエージェントに分ける
・レビュー役には実装役と違うモデルを当て、「どこが間違っているか」だけを探させる
・親エージェントには作業をさせず、進捗の監視とマージの判断だけを任せる
・合格条件は文章ではなく、テストや出力の比較のように機械で判定できる形にしておく

ツールを古い言語から移したい、遅いスクリプトを書き直したい、という場面なら、まず比較テストだけ用意して、小さな部品1つで試すのが現実的です。

エージェントの性能差は、モデルよりも「何をもって正解とするか」をどれだけ機械に渡せるかで開いていく。今回の2,209体は、そのことをかなりはっきり見せた事例だと思います。

Playing with Public Health: Multinational Profits and the Health Crisis of Indian Youth

Today, the health of our country's youth and children stands at a critical crossroads. Major American multinational corporations such as PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, and McDonald's are reaching homes across the Indian market through aggressive advertisements and enticing marketing of their ultra-processed foods and cold drinks. In their blind race for profits, these companies have complete disregard for how their products are hollowing out the health of our nation's future generations.

The Deadly Trap of Junk Food and Cold Drinks.

The food products sold by these companies contain excessive amounts of refined sugar, salt, unhealthy fats, and harmful chemicals. Through attractive advertisements and celebrity endorsements, they are marketed in such a way that today's youth generation considers them symbols of a modern lifestyle. 

As a result:
Early-Onset Diseases: Diseases like Type-2 diabetes, hypertension, and fatty liver disease are rapidly spreading among children and adolescents—conditions that were once considered problems exclusive to the elderly.

Obesity Epidemic: Driven by the consumption of calorie-dense yet nutrition-devoid products, childhood obesity is assuming a alarming shape, which drastically multiplies the risk of cardiovascular diseases later in life.
Deceptive Marketing: These companies advertise their products as "energy boosters" or "healthy snacks," whereas reality is completely the reverse.

The Urgent Need for Policy and Social Intervention.

Health is a fundamental human right and cannot be sacrificed at the altar of corporate profits. To combat this grave situation, we must consider the following steps:
Strict Advertising Regulations: Legal bans or stringent controls should be enforced on advertisements of junk food and cold drinks targeting children.

Warning Labels: Similar to tobacco and alcohol, clear and prominent health warning labels should be made mandatory on the packaging of processed foods high in sugar, sodium, and fat.

Awareness Campaigns: Comprehensive campaigns must be launched across schools, colleges, and community levels to promote traditional and nutritious Indian diets.
Profit can never be greater than humanity and health. The time has come to protect our younger generation from the commercial conspiracies of these multinational corporations and take concrete steps toward building a healthy and empowered India.

records.text:
📍 加密市場大清算、能源政策急轉：真正要看的是誰還在買、誰真的能供貨｜叮叮跨市場筆記

截至：2026/10/10 09:00（UTC+8）

今天先抓三件事：

• 加密市場出現約 11.9 億美元槓桿清算，ETH 特別承壓，但第一個觸發點仍未確認。

• 美國正式放寬部分俄羅斯柴油交易限制；同時，颶風迫使墨西哥灣大量油氣停產。

• 大型 ETH 持有者 BitMine 接近 5% 持有上限，市場必須重新思考未來買盤能持續多久。

───

目前我的態度：

加密市場的急跌與清算是真實發生的，但現在不能把任何一條利空新聞指定為唯一原因。

能源市場則同時出現增加供應的政策承諾，與已經發生的停產。

短期判斷取決於兩件事：加密市場的被迫平倉能否降溫，以及能源供應能否真正恢復或增加。

歷史資訊重建，非即時交易訊號。

───

【市場現在怎麼看？】

Crypto：

BTC：

先跌，再反彈。已公開的行情顯示，BTC 一度從約 83,200 美元跌至約 80,400 美元，之後回到約 82,200 美元附近。

美國 BTC 現貨 ETF 在先前交易日出現資金淨流出。不過，這仍不能證明 ETF 贖回就是第一波急跌的觸發點。

───

ETH：

ETH 是這次槓桿清算的重要受災區。統計截面顯示，ETH 清算金額約 3.56 億美元，高於 BTC 的約 2.98 億美元。

更值得追蹤的是 BitMine：它已接近原定持有 ETH 總供給 5% 的目標，而主席明言不會繼續累積超過這個上限。

───

SOL：

同一波清算中，SOL 約有 7,100 萬美元槓桿部位遭平倉。

美國 SOL 相關 ETF 在 10 月 8 日交易日有淨流出紀錄。但本批未找到能獨立證明 SOL 網路或機構需求發生重大轉折的新事件。

───

NEAR：

NEAR 的走勢與其他幣有明顯分化。台灣時間 10 月 10 日上午公布的一份行情分析，記錄其此前 24 小時反彈約 9.8%。

Bitwise 的美國 NEAR 現貨產品早在 9 月 29 日就已上市，不是今天突然獲准。

新跨鏈工具有媒體報導，但真實交易量、收入與新增 NEAR 需求，仍待驗證。

───

美股：

美國 10 月 9 日收盤，S&P 500 漲 0.59%，Nasdaq 漲 0.64%，Dow 漲 0.83%。

因此，這不是所有風險資產同步崩跌的一天。市場內部仍有差異，部分半導體和傳統電信股承壓，其他板塊則上漲。

───

原油：

Brent 週五收在約每桶 104.72 美元，WTI 約 91.85 美元，雙雙小幅上漲。

颶風來襲前，墨西哥灣已有約每日 150 萬桶的原油產能預防性關閉。這是實際供應減少，不只是氣象預報。

───

黃金：

現貨黃金在台灣時間 10 月 10 日凌晨約為每盎司 4,194 美元，當時上漲約 1.5%；白銀亦走高。

油價、利率、美元及地緣政治同時牽動貴金屬，現在不宜把漲幅全部歸因於單一避險消息。

───

其他重大事件：

美國財政部已發布俄羅斯柴油相關交易許可，配合美俄宣布的柴油供應安排。

這是實際政策轉向，直接關係到全球精煉燃料供應，也涉及對俄制裁的執行方向。

───

【主線｜加密市場先急跌，清算把跌勢放大，但第一個觸發點仍待確認】

先看行情。

美東時間 10 月 8 日晚間，加密市場出現急跌，BTC 一度接近 80,400 美元。隨後市場反彈，部分空頭也遭到平倉。

因此，這不是只有單向下跌的簡單故事。

───

再看槓桿。

10 月 9 日中午以前已公布的統計顯示，前 24 小時加密市場約有 11.9 億美元槓桿清算，其中超過 10 億美元是偏多部位。

當價格跌破槓桿交易者能承受的範圍，平台會強制平倉，讓原本的跌勢被進一步放大。

───

這裡有四種不同的線索。

利率與地緣政治，是持續背景。

ETF 淨流出，是可以追蹤的資金壓力。

大型 ETH 買家未來可能停止增持，是結構性需求變化。

槓桿清算，則是已確認的價格放大器。

目前還缺足夠證據，把其中任何一項認定為最初引爆行情的事件。

───

下一步要看的是：強制平倉是否減少、未平倉合約是否穩定、現貨買賣深度是否恢復。

如果只是空頭回補造成反彈，但現貨需求沒有改善，市場仍可能再次劇烈震盪。

───

【主線｜俄羅斯柴油供應有了政策突破，但墨西哥灣真的在停產】

美國宣布與俄羅斯達成柴油供應安排，並由財政部發布相關交易許可。

美方提出的第一批規模超過 30 萬公噸，後續還有追加安排。

消息出現後，柴油期貨一度明顯下跌。

───

但另一邊，颶風 Isaias 迫使墨西哥灣生產商提前撤離人員、關閉設施。

約七成當地離岸原油產能暫時停產，這已經影響供應。

一邊是允許更多燃料進入市場的政策變化，一邊是現有產能暫時退出。

真正重要的是兩者何時轉化成實際供貨。

───

這也是為什麼不能只看原油一個報價。

柴油是精煉後的產品，原油是煉油原料。

俄羅斯柴油的許可與供應承諾，最直接影響的是柴油市場；颶風則直接影響美國離岸油氣生產。

接下來要看到實際裝運、到貨與復產，才能判斷供應緊張是否真正緩解。

───

【主線｜大型 ETH 買家接近上限，市場要看的是下一段需求】

BitMine 先前披露持有約 601.64 萬枚 ETH，約佔當時總供給 4.9%。

10 月 7 日，主席 Tom Lee 說明，公司不會持有超過 ETH 總供給 5%。

這讓原本的累積目標，同時成為未來買入的上限。

───

假如某個大型買家過去持續進場，市場就可能逐漸習慣這股新增需求。

一旦這個買家接近目標，即使它不賣出任何一枚 ETH，未來的買盤也可能減少。

對市場來說，「不再增加需求」本身就值得觀察。

───

但這項說法出現在本批研究之前，不能倒過來直接說它引發了 10 月 9 日的急跌。

而且，接近上限、宣布停止增持、真正停止增持，以及出售現有持倉，是四件不同的事。

下一次正式持倉披露，會比市場猜測更有意義。

───

【現在還不能下哪些結論？】

• 約 11.9 億美元清算，不代表同額資金離開加密市場。

• 清算可以放大下跌，但本次尚無法確認它之前的第一個觸發事件。

• ETF 某天淨流出，不代表所有機構都在賣；週末沒有新交易，也不能寫成零流入。

• BitMine 接近停止增持，不代表已經出售現有 ETH。

• 俄羅斯柴油交易獲得許可，不代表宣布的數量已全部裝船或送達。

• NEAR 的 ETF、Intents、AI 或跨鏈活動，不會自動變成 NEAR 代幣的新增淨買盤。

• HOT Bridge 相關歷史安全事故，也不能直接寫成 NEAR Protocol 主網遭駭。

───

【接下來看什麼？】

第一，加密市場接下來 24～72 小時的清算、未平倉合約與交易深度。

Is this how you are doing it? Do you use Ubuntu linux?

The poster’s actual method (two Linux laptops: one online for building/broadcasting, one offline for signing) is a standard air-gapped workflow that avoids trusting any vendor device. Here is a practical version for Kaspa, based on rusty-kaspa CLI and related tools.

1. Prepare the offline signing laptop (do this first, carefully)
•  Use a dedicated or freshly wiped laptop. Prefer one where you can physically remove the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth modules or permanently disable them in BIOS + blacklist kernel modules.
•  Install a minimal Linux (Ubuntu/Debian or similar). Enable full-disk LUKS encryption during install. Refuse all online accounts, telemetry, and Livepatch.
•  Never connect this machine to any network after setup. Transfer software (rusty-kaspa binaries or source) via verified USB from a clean source.
•  Generate your seed phrase only on this machine. Record it offline (metal backup preferred). Derive and export only the extended public key (kpub) for use elsewhere.

2. Prepare the online laptop (watch-only / build & broadcast)
•  Run a normal Linux setup with network access. Install rusty-kaspa (kaspad + kaspa-wallet / CLI).
•  Import the wallet in watch-only mode using only the kpub (no private keys or seed). Sync a node (or connect to one) so you have current UTXOs.
•  Build unsigned transactions with the CLI (examples from Kaspa wiki/docs): create an unsigned transaction specifying destination, amount, and source addresses derived from the public key. Export the unsigned data (text/JSON/hex).

3. Signing and broadcast workflow
•  Transfer the unsigned transaction to the offline laptop via a clean USB stick (or QR if your tools support it). Prefer a dedicated stick you wipe or use read-only where possible.
•  On the offline machine: load the unsigned transaction, verify the destination address, amount, and fees on screen, then sign with the local private key. Export the signed transaction.
•  Transfer the signed transaction back to the online laptop and broadcast it (kaspa-wallet broadcast or equivalent). Confirm on-chain.
•  Practice the full flow with tiny amounts first. Mistakes in address verification or transfer media are the main real risks.
Practical notes and alternatives
•  Older Kaspa offline flows sometimes required copying a node database for UTXO data; current CLI approaches with public-key import + unsigned transaction creation reduce that. Check the latest rusty-kaspa / kaspa-ng docs for exact commands, as partial signing (PSKT-like) support has improved.
•  For a more hardware-oriented air-gap, look at open-source projects like KasSigner (ESP32-S3 based, QR-only transfer, Rust, no persistent keys). These avoid a full second laptop but are experimental.
•  USB transfer has residual risks (malware on the stick); QR or microSD with careful verification is cleaner when available. Always double-check every address and amount on the offline screen before signing.
•  Seed backup and recovery testing are essential—lose the seed and the funds are gone, regardless of the setup.
This method gives strong isolation at the cost of convenience and requires discipline. For most holders, a reputable hardware wallet (with physical access controls and a strong PIN) is simpler; the dual-laptop route is for those who want to eliminate vendor trust entirely. Always verify software hashes and start small.

In this hypothetical, a pure bot-as-CEO structure is not legally available in most jurisdictions because directors and officers must be natural persons who can hold duties and face accountability. A workable approximation is an LLC or similar entity whose operating agreement routes operational decisions to an AI or software agent, while a human (the “Joe” proxy) serves as the formal manager, nominee director, or residual signatory who accepts legal liability and control obligations.

A reasonable cost estimate for that human role, paid in USDC, would likely fall in the range of several thousand to low tens of thousands of dollars per year under ordinary conditions. Standard nominee-director services in places such as the BVI, Cayman, Seychelles, or Singapore commonly run roughly $1,000–$5,000 annually plus a security deposit, secretarial fees, and occasional per-action charges. Adding crypto exposure, experimental AI governance, or the novelty and regulatory uncertainty of a space-hosted project would push the figure higher—potentially $10,000–$30,000+ per year once risk premiums, indemnification, insurance, and limited operational involvement are included. The exact number depends on the jurisdiction chosen, how active the human must be, the human’s personal risk tolerance, and whether the arrangement is purely formal or involves ongoing judgment calls. There is no single market clearing price; it would be negotiated like any other high-trust professional service.

For tax domicile, low-or-zero corporate tax options such as Cayman, BVI, or certain UAE free zones are the usual candidates for a tech or protocol-style project, provided economic-substance and beneficial-ownership rules can be met. Estonia-style 0% tax on retained earnings or Singapore startup reliefs are alternatives when banking or treaty access matters more. The optimal choice turns on the actual revenue model, founders’ personal residence, and whether the entity needs regulated status.

A space-based data center would not be governed by maritime law. It would fall under the Outer Space Treaty framework: the state that registers the object keeps jurisdiction and control, launching states authorize and supervise private activities, and international liability rules apply to damage. Data-protection and other terrestrial regulations typically follow the operator rather than the orbital location of the servers.

書生：【又多一人．事前並無消息】 警方起訴 52 歲男子發煽動信息今提堂，拘捕行動來自 7 月

據多間港媒報道，國安處 10 月 7 日控告一名 52 歲男子發布煽動刊物，今午在西九龍裁判法院提堂。

值得注意的是，不少傳媒都以「國安拘捕一名 52 歲本地男子」為標題，報道事件。但閱讀內容會發現，是次拘捕行動是國安在今年 7 月 9 日在東區採取的拘捕行動。

書生翻查網上新聞資料，找不到任何國安拘捕行動的訊息。換句話說，國安的一些拘捕行動是非公開的，傳媒與公眾均不知情。

根據過往紀錄，國安對知名社運或政界人物的拘捕行動，通常都是相當高調，甚至有跡象顯示事前會找親建制傳媒（例如星島），在拘捕當日大肆拍攝及報道。相反，無名無姓，沒有任何傳媒「爆料」的，通常都是知名度不高的星斗市民。

但這些市民發布了什麼煽動刊物，階層、姓名、職業，一概沒有人清楚。他們未來將會面對怎樣的困境，也無法被關注。

自國安法生效後，國安總共拘捕了至少 410 人。對比新聞資料後，其中至少 10% 的拘捕行動是沒有公開進行。

事件凸顯出，國安針對普通市民網上言論的執法行動愈來愈頻繁，而且公眾並不知情。

警方近月多次「提醒市民」，煽動屬嚴重罪行，首次定罪可被判處監禁 7 年。但既然煽動屬嚴重罪行，警方理應及早公布相關行動，具體涉案的言論，讓公眾知情，避免誤墮法網。

Your next SaaS customer might be an AI agent.

@kushalbyatnal shared that an Instinct agent signed itself up for Extend, completed onboarding, obtained API access, and started using the product.

I think more SaaS companies need to prepare for this.

Most products still expect a human to:

Open a website
Create an account
Complete onboarding
Find the documentation
Generate an API key
Configure the integration
Extend has started building a different path.
Its agent quickstart supports MCP, CLI, agent skills, SDK context files, and machine-readable documentation.
The CLI can install a SKILL.md file that teaches coding agents how to use its commands.
The MCP server exposes product operations and structured errors.
Agents can read documentation as Markdown instead of parsing a website.

This matters for anyone building developer tools or SaaS products.

I would start with three things:

Make your API easy to discover. Give agents clear documentation and predictable tool interfaces.

Make authentication safe for machines. Use scoped credentials and explicit permissions.

Make failures easy to fix. Return structured errors that tell agents what went wrong.

The reported Instinct signup is one example. The broader opportunity is making software easier for autonomous agents to operate.

1/ 先说结论：欧洲AI的“主权之作”来了。Mistral Large 4（内部代号ML4）10月6日开启公测，是美国和中国之外第一个万亿参数开放权重模型。参数：1.05万亿总量、52B激活（MoE架构）、1.6B视觉编码器原生多模态、100万token上下文、160+语言覆盖全部欧盟官方语言。

2/ 训练配置：约3800块NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPU，欧洲本土数据中心，从零训练约2个月。这不是租美国算力微调的“欧洲贴牌”，而是端到端在欧盟司法管辖下训出来的——对GDPR、AI法案、数据主权敏感的客户，这是架构级卖点。

3/ 跑分（多为官方宣称，理性看待）：
- 网络安全是它最强的垂直领域：Cybench 93%，漏洞复现+修复测试82%全场最高。最有节目效果的是：Claude Opus 5.5和GPT-6 Astra在这项直接拒绝作答，接近0分——不是做不出来，是不让做
- 代码：DeepSWE v1.1 61.7%，Coding Agent Index 49.8%（超DeepSeek V4 Pro、Qwen3.8 Max）
- 人类盲测：Surge AI 3.74/5，仅次于Claude Opus 5（4.22）
- 金融：Finance Agent v2 54.7，超GPT-6 Astra（53.5）
- 视觉定位：Dense200 42% vs GPT-6 Astra 41%——少数开放模型单项正面超过闭源旗舰

4/ 价格：官方价输入$1.36/百万token、输出$4.18/百万token；公测期半价$0.68/$2.09。横向对比：约Claude Opus 5.5的三分之一到五分之一，GPT-6 Astra的七分之一到十二分之一。万亿参数卖出中端价，全靠MoE每次只激活5%参数。

5/ 开源这件事，先泼盆冷水：
- 权重承诺10月底发布（有报道称10月27日），但协议是自定义license，不是Apache 2.0
- “开放权重”≠“可商用”：商用前务必读license原文
- 部署门槛：1万亿参数要全量进内存，本地部署硬件账单很贵，大部分团队还是走API

6/ 「Le Chonk」梗的出处：今年6月，Reddit和X网友虚构了一个“Le Chaton Fat”（肥猫）模型，还P了假跑分图宣称打败Claude。CEO Arthur Mensch亲自下场玩梗，官网加了只卡通猫。这次官方通告里“非常正式地”写着：le Chonk。玩梗玩成了官方命名，AI圈整活天花板。

7/ 为什么重要：2026年开放权重前沿基本是“中国vs其他所有人”的格局，Mistral把自己定位成“中国之外最强的开放权重”。主权AI是真生意：沙特HUMAIN 8月签了数亿欧元大单；9月三星领投€30亿D轮，估值超€210亿。

NO — Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, 2025. The Senate cloture vote failed 51–45. 
NO — H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, final Senate passage in 2025. 
NO — an H.R. 1 amendment dealing with enhanced Medicaid funding and state coverage of certain nonqualified immigrants. 
NO — 2026 proposal establishing federal voter-registration ID, photo-ID voting requirements, and election-day/counting rules. 
NO — 2026 cloture vote on S. 5271, which would require photo identification for voting under the Help America Vote Act. 
NO — another 2026 women’s-sports amendment seeking protections based on sex in athletics. 
NO — Secure America Act, S. 2 — June 5, 2026 

Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act — S.9: Kelly voted NO on cloture on the motion to proceed on March 3, 2025. The vote was 51–45, short of the 60 votes then required, so the bill did not advance. 
H.R.1968 — FY2025 government funding: Kelly voted NO on cloture March 14, 2025. Cloture nevertheless passed 62–38. 
GENIUS Act/stablecoin legislation — S.1582: Kelly voted NO on cloture on the motion to proceed May 8, 2025. The vote failed 48–49. 
Eliminate Shutdowns Act — S.2806: Kelly voted NO on the motion to advance the bill September 29, 2025. Cloture failed 37–61. 
FY2026 continuing appropriations — H.R.5371: Kelly voted NO on repeated attempts to advance the funding bill during the October 2025 shutdown fight; several cloture votes failed because they did not reach 60. 
Pay for federal employees working during a shutdown — S.3012: Kelly voted NO on cloture on the motion to proceed November 7, 2025. It failed 53–43 because 60 votes were required. 
Health Savings Account / health-cost bill — S.3386: Kelly voted NO on cloture on the motion to proceed December 11, 2025. The motion failed 51–48. 
FY2026 appropriations — H.R.7147: Kelly was among the NO votes on attempts to advance the bill in February and March 2026; the motions failed to reach 60. 

Pete Hegseth
Military recruiting rebounded sharply. By 2026 the Pentagon was reporting very strong enlistment numbers, after years of recruiting difficulties. Even the Washington Post noted the administration’s claim of record recruiting across the services.  
He made combat readiness, physical standards and merit central priorities, ordering reviews of standards and emphasizing advancement based on performance and ability.  
He welcomed back service members separated over the COVID vaccine mandate, part of the administration’s effort to allow those troops to return to service.  
He launched a major overhaul of Pentagon weapons procurement. The goal has been to get weapons and technology to troops faster, increase competition and reduce the notoriously slow acquisition bureaucracy.  
He pushed drone and counter-drone modernization, including efforts to get American-made drones into troops’ hands more rapidly.  
He accelerated military use of artificial intelligence and modern software, including department-wide AI projects and changes to software acquisition.  
He pushed allies toward carrying more of the defense burden rather than leaving the United States responsible for a disproportionate share. That’s been a major element of the administration’s NATO strategy.
He worked on strengthening the defense industrial base—increasing production capacity and reducing barriers that slow companies supplying the military.

三星把130亿参数的大模型，压成了不到1GB
LittleBit：每个权重平均 0.1 比特，S1哥的旧手机终于看到了跑大模型的希望。

S1哥的电脑硬盘，常年处于”红条”状态。不是因为我存了什么好东西，是因为我下了一堆本地大模型，每一个都十几个 G，跑起来风扇像要起飞，跑完一个问题，我泡的面都坨了。

所以 10 月 8 日刷到 @thesupermannx 这条推，S1哥第一时间去查了原论文：

三星开源了一种方法，能把 130 亿参数的大模型压到 1GB 以内，名字叫 LittleBit。

S1哥核实了一下：这是三星研究院（Samsung Research）的论文《LittleBit: Ultra Low-Bit Quantization via Latent Factorization》，2025 年 5 月就挂上了 arXiv，后来入选 NeurIPS 2025，GitHub 上有官方代码（SamsungLabs/LittleBit）。论文原话是：目标做到每个权重 0.1 比特（0.1 BPW），内存减少约 31 倍，比如把 Llama2-13B 压到 0.9GB 以下。

所以严格说，这不是”刚刚发布”，而是一篇被重新翻红的论文。但不妨碍它很猛。

（原推：@thesupermannx，据推文页面约 4400 赞；论文：https://t.co/R38QO5XbEj）

一、演出来：把一头大象塞进一块方糖

正常一个大模型的每个权重，用 16 位浮点数存（FP16）。你可以把它理解成：每个参数都要占一个大格子。

现在压缩界常见的玩法是 4 比特、2 比特，已经算”挤一挤”。而 LittleBit 直接冲到”平均每个权重不到 1 比特”，某些配置做到 0.1 比特。

这是什么概念？相当于原来一个人住一间房，现在是十个人共用一个床位——还要求他们第二天起来，干活不能出错。

它的核心思路，按论文说法是：先把权重矩阵做低秩的”潜在分解”（latent factorization），再把分解出来的因子二值化，只留正负号；然后用行、列、潜在维度上的多尺度补偿，把丢掉的信息尽量找回来。原推把这概括成”用简单的符号翻转/XOR 代替复杂的矩阵乘法”。

二、挖本质：压缩的极限，在挑战”大模型必须很贵”这个假设

原推里那个最吸睛的数字是”推理加速 11.6 倍”。S1哥得帮大家拆一下：

论文写的是”潜在的 11.6 倍加速”，NeurIPS 的展示材料里写的是”最高 11.6 倍的内核加速，测于 RTX 4090”。而三星研究院的官方博客里，端到端的实测例子是比 FP16 快约 2.46 倍。

也就是说：11.6 倍是某个计算环节的峰值，不是你整体用起来就快 11 倍。原推说得有点”满”，但方向没错。

本质在于：过去大家默认”想要更强的模型，就得更多显存、更贵的卡”。LittleBit 这类研究在问另一个问题——如果把模型压到极致，还能不能用？ 论文给的答案是：在 Llama2-7B 上，它 0.1 比特的表现，超过了此前领先方法 0.7 比特的表现。

三、放大：对行业和普通人意味着什么

对手机和端侧厂商：三星自己就是做手机的，这事儿的潜台词不言自明——大模型未来会更多地跑在你的设备里，而不是全部依赖云端。

对开发者：显存不再是唯一门槛。便宜设备、旧显卡、边缘设备，都有机会跑起以前跑不动的模型。

对普通人：隐私和离线能力。模型在本地跑，你的数据不用上传，没网也能用。

当然，S1哥也要说句公道话：论文实验主要基于 Llama2 这类模型，压缩到 0.1 比特后的能力损失、在新模型上的效果、实际产品里能不能落地，都还需要时间验证。

结尾

所以 S1哥决定先不删硬盘里那堆十几 G 的模型了——万一哪天它们都能压成 1G，我就能多存十倍的模型，然后继续一个都不用。

模型可以压缩到 0.1 比特，那我们每天刷手机时那点注意力，是不是早就被压得比它还小了？

你最想在手机上离线跑一个什么样的 AI？评论区说说，S1哥帮你看看现在有没有能用的。

#三星 #LittleBit #模型量化 #端侧AI #S1哥说AI

【美股雷达｜盘后分析📊（10/9）】

周五美股全线收涨，三大指数回补周四科技股的抛压，标普500收在7,811.51点，距离周二刚创下的历史高位仅一步之遥。结构上也有改善：11个板块中9个上涨，涨势不再只靠大型科技股支撑。

但芯片依然偏弱，10年期美债收益率仍停在5.25%一线。这更像是业绩季前的风险偏好修复，而不是趋势已经反转。

周五收盘（美东时间）：

📈道指 51,655.01（+423.37点，+0.83%）

📈标普500 7,811.51（+46.15点，+0.59%）

📈纳指 27,366.17（+172.83点，+0.64%）

📈罗素2000 2,808.57（+14.45点，+0.52%）

本周累计：道指+1.15%，标普500+0.95%，纳指+0.19%，罗素2000-0.91%，是四大指数中唯一收跌的。

本周的核心矛盾是：

高油价、高利率与AI估值担忧并存，周四纳指因OpenAI营收数据不及预期而重挫，周五只是部分修复；

大盘价值与防御方向更强，纳指和小盘股的周度表现落后；

下周CPI与银行财报密集登场，市场在数据前选择先回补仓位。

美债收益率（周五全天上行）：

2年期约4.80%，+3.9bp；

10年期约5.25%，+1.5bp；

30年期约5.61%，基本持平。

短端涨幅大于长端，2s10s利差约45bp，曲线小幅走平，说明市场仍在消化Fed继续加息的可能。10年期收益率距离本周触及的2002年以来高位不远，这依然是压制高估值成长股的主要变量。

周一为哥伦布日，股市正常交易，债市休市，下一次有效的收益率定价要等到周二。

跨资产表现：

美元指数约102.0，基本持平；

黄金约4,216，+1.43%；

白银约61.05，+2.73%；

WTI原油约91.85，+0.39%；

布伦特原油约104.72，+0.42%。

特朗普表示美国在中期选举前不会攻击伊朗，盘初油价一度回落，但中东局势和墨西哥湾飓风造成的原油减产，让油价收盘仍小幅收红。黄金白银同步走强，说明避险和通胀对冲需求没有降温。

板块表现：

房地产板块：+1.85%，领涨；

医疗保健板块：+1.48%，位居第二；

科技板块：+0.4%，跑输大盘但收红；

能源板块：小幅收跌；

通信服务板块：收跌，被电信股拖累；

费城半导体指数：-0.4%。

11个板块中9个上涨，其中只有可选消费一个大型成长板块进入涨幅前列，说明本轮反弹的结构比周四健康。

盘中重点个股：

 $HUM 哈门那：大涨逾10%，CMS恢复其旗舰医保优势计划4星评级。

 $MRNA 莫德纳：+14.2%，并重新进入纳斯达克100指数。

 $NVAX 诺瓦瓦克斯：+15.8%，NIH拟推进个性化癌症疫苗研发的消息提振生物医药。

 $CCI 冠城国际：涨超10%，作为通信基础设施REIT受益于SpaceX的频谱收购。

 $TMUS T-Mobile：盘中跌幅一度超12%。

 $VZ 威瑞森、 $T 美国电话电报：同步重挫，市场担心SpaceX收购约80亿美元的低频段频谱后进军移动业务，冲击传统运营商格局。

 $NVDA：-0.5%。

 $MU 美光科技：-0.7%。

 $AMD 超威半导体：-2.0%。

 $AAPL：受订单削减报道拖累，早盘走弱。

 $HPQ 惠普：盘中一度跌超6%，公司预计2027年全球PC出货量将出现中个位数下滑。

 $DAL 达美航空：三季度业绩不及预期，为两年来首次，并大幅下调全年盈利指引，高油价压力继续体现。

今天最值得注意的是：

芯片股连续两天偏弱，但大盘并没有被带下水，说明资金正从AI硬件向医疗、地产和价值方向分流；

 $TMUS 、 $VZ 、 $T 的集体下挫是事件驱动的板块重估，与宏观无关；

密歇根大学消费者信心初值降至46.3，低于预期的47.6，高利率与高油价正在压制居民信心，但股市并未因此走弱。

今天的市场主线可以概括为：

业绩季前资金回补大盘与防御板块，芯片与电信承压；指数逼近前高，但高利率和高油价的约束没有解除。

下周关键日程：

周一（10/12）：股市正常交易，债市休市；

周二（10/13）：摩根大通、高盛、富国银行、花旗等大型银行发布三季报，业绩季正式展开；

周三（10/14）：9月CPI，决定Fed能否在加息后暂停。

操作参考：

📌 CPI是下周最大的单日变量。如果通胀降温、10年期收益率回落到5.25%下方，科技和芯片有机会修复估值；若数据偏热，需要警惕收益率再度冲击5.30%上方的高位。

📌 银行财报是业绩季的第一块试金石。重点看净利息收入指引、信贷成本和投行业务收入，如果几家大行表现一致偏强，金融板块的领涨逻辑会得到巩固；若指引保守，近期的价值轮动需要重新评估。

📌 芯片方向的关键是止跌信号。如果费城半导体指数周一能够企稳，说明周四的OpenAI冲击已被消化；如果继续走弱，说明资金对AI硬件估值的担忧在升级。

📌 地缘与天气带来油价波动。伊朗谈判进展、霍尔木兹海峡局势和墨西哥湾减产恢复的节奏，都会影响能源与航空板块的相对强弱。

📌 周一债市休市，美债定价缺席，股市容易出现缺少利率锚点的波动，周二银行财报和周三CPI才是真正的定价时刻。

下周一值得关注的标的：

1️⃣ $JPM 摩根大通：周二盘前发布三季报，是整个业绩季的风向标，重点看净利息收入与信贷成本。

2️⃣ $HUM 哈门那：医保优势计划评级恢复带来大幅跳涨，关注上涨能否持续，还是出现获利回吐。

本機跑 120B 模型，Windows 筆電的競爭焦點正在換軌
Microsoft 開放預購 Surface Laptop Ultra，最高配備 128GB 統一記憶體與 NVIDIA RTX Spark，可在本機執行超過 120B 參數的 AI 模型。這讓 Windows 筆電不再只比遊戲與傳統生產力，也開始比誰能容納更大的本機 AI。

RTX Spark 將 Blackwell RTX GPU、Grace CPU 與統一記憶體整合在同一平台。Surface Laptop Ultra 最高有 20 核心 Grace CPU、6,144 個 GPU Core、128GB 統一記憶體，Microsoft 表示其 AI 算力最高可達 1 PFLOP。與系統 RAM、GPU VRAM 分離的常見筆電架構相比，CPU 與 GPU 共用大容量記憶體，對需要載入大量權重的 LLM 與生成式 AI 特別關鍵。

Windows 也將強化「Hybrid Intelligence」：適合的工作交給本機 CPU、GPU 或 NPU，需要更大模型時再轉往雲端。Windows ML 新增 llama.cpp 支援，讓開發者能更直接運用 Windows 硬體執行 GGUF 等開源模型。Microsoft 展示的 MAI Code 1.1 Flash 總參數為 137B，但每次推論約啟用 6.8B；經 3-bit 量化後，模型容量可降低接近 80%，並支援最高 256K Context。

Copilot 未來在使用者授權下，可讀取相關檔案與近期工作內容，協助整理、診斷、排錯、寫程式與執行部分 Windows 操作。為限制 Agent 權限，Microsoft 推出隔離執行環境 Microsoft Execution Containers（MXC），並列出 Claude Code、Hermes Agent、Manus、Perplexity 等支援陣容。

Microsoft 對 MacBook Pro M5 Pro 提出的首 Token、AI 圖像與影片生成比較，屬特定測試條件下的官方數據，實際表現仍取決於模型、軟體與硬體配置。較值得注意的是，128GB 統一記憶體與 Windows ML 導入 llama.cpp，可能讓「可在本機跑多大模型」成為 Windows PC 的新規格戰場。對你的工作流程而言，本機 AI 的隱私、延遲與離線能力，是否值得為這類硬體升級？

观察员早报 · 10月10日

周五美股三大指数集体收涨，道指涨0.83%报51654.95点，标普500涨0.59%报7811.51点，纳指涨0.64%报27366.17点，三大指数周线均收涨。前一天OpenAI营收口径引发的AI回报疑虑，被"年底年化营收达700亿美元"的预期部分缓解，资金重新回到科技股。BTC报82529美元，24小时涨1.1%，ETH约2486美元，ZEC约1211美元，前两天的8.3万到7.9万承接区间暂时守住。

先看市场结构，这次反弹有一个细节值得记。AI应用软件股涨得最猛，Snowflake、Datadog大涨7%，Palantir涨超5%，亚马逊涨3.29%，微软涨2.38%；但英伟达跌0.52%，半导体ETF跌0.65%。资金从"卖铲子"的芯片转向"用AI赚钱"的软件和云，这和伯恩斯坦此前说的"AI智能体把需求从GPU扩展到数据库、软件平台"是同一个方向。苹果跌1.1%，原因是据报要求供应商削减iPhone 18 Pro系列的零部件订单，被解读为存储成本上涨加提价抑制了需求。

油价和地缘方面，特朗普称与普京通话"非常成功"，俄罗斯将立即向美国及全球市场供应超过30万吨柴油，11月再供应50万吨，随后再供应100万吨，美股随后升至日内高点。但油价当天仍小幅收高，WTI约92美元，布伦特在104美元上方。这条消息要分开看：柴油是前面一直紧张的成品油环节，增供有针对性；但这是特朗普单方面发文，具体合同、运输和制裁安排尚未披露，兑现程度要观察。Baird的分析师说得很直接，白宫和中东各方不断传出相互矛盾的消息，市场很难形成明确方向，所以反弹力度温和。

利率方面，10年期美债收益率周五约5.24%，低于周三的24年来高位，但仍很高。这里有一条值得单独记：CFTC数据显示，截至10月6日的两周内，资产管理机构持有的超长期国债期货净多头仓位按每基点风险计减少约2700万美元，相当于约380亿美元的10年期现券规模，同期30年期收益率升到24年高点5.68%。这被解读为被迫抛售的迹象，也就是长端利率的上行里，有一部分是去杠杆造成的，而不只是基本面。这和美银说"美债重新具备竞争力"、TLT看涨期权成交增加的背景并不矛盾：有人在高位抄底，也有人被迫卖出。

下周是密集的数据和财报窗口：10月14日公布9月CPI，巴克莱和摩根士丹利预计核心CPI环比0.24%、整体同比约3.7%；10月16日沃什在曼谷讲话；大型银行财报开始，包括富国、高盛、花旗、摩根大通、美国银行和摩根士丹利。LSEG预计标普500三季度盈利同比增长30.6%，能源和科技分别增长123%和66.5%。

其他美股：SpaceX收购800MHz频谱的消息持续发酵，T-Mobile收跌超13%，AT&T跌近10%，Verizon跌8.7%，比盘前的跌幅更大，市场认为这对运营商是直接挑战。Moderna涨14.2%、诺瓦瓦克斯涨15.8%，起因是NIH据称在推进癌症疫苗相关工作，仍是"据称"的消息。哈门那涨11.6%，因为其2027年医保优势计划95%的参保人所在计划获四星或以上评级。美光扩大回购授权至351.6亿美元，12月9日起生效，此前100亿美元计划还剩约22亿美元额度，美光年内累计涨约260%。达美航空下调全年指引至每股5.10到5.60美元，燃油支出同比增62%，预计全年燃油成本多约60亿美元，但CEO称提价没有削弱旅客预订意愿。

加密和政策方面，信息量也不小。

CFTC发布拟议规则，拟把体育、政治、文化和天气类事件合约明确纳入"互换"定义，主席Selig称其属于商品衍生品、归CFTC专属管辖，征求意见30天；同日临时最终规则明确体育博彩、赌场游戏不属于互换。预测市场正在被纳入联邦监管。Telegram把Gram钱包更名为Money，向全平台超过十亿用户开放，配套交易平台Walt提供300多种资产，包括代币化股票、贵金属、永续合约。分发渠道的体量很大，但用户真正使用的比例是另一回事。

风险方面有三条要谨慎看待。一是Ledger用户疑似遭大规模盗币，据链上分析师Specter称，资金来自数百个受害者钱包，累计损失超8600万美元，但攻击原因、受影响人数和Ledger是否存在漏洞都未证实，目前只是链上追踪加社区报告，不宜下结论。二是美国司法部在审查币安是否遵守2023年和解协议，消息很短，细节未披露。三是美国政府相关钱包三天内向Coinbase Prime存入17733枚BTC和750枚WBTC，约合16亿美元，存入不等于卖出，但政府钱包仍持有约254亿美元，这笔抛压预期需要留意。另外贝森特称美国本周可能查扣约10亿美元与伊朗相关的加密货币，政策已从"极限施压"转向"绝对孤立"，这是官员口头表态，尚无执行细节。

【今日市場重點｜2026-10-09】

今日有兩條主線：

加拿大勞動市場重新轉弱；同時，能源風險與接近二十六年高位嘅長債收益率，繼續提高政府及企業融資成本。

AI需求未見崩塌，但資本開始更仔細分辨估值、現金流與執行能力。由今期開始，AI Dashboard改為每週更新；平日只有出現重大新證據先另行跟進。

【美國長債｜需求正常，但資金價格仍然高】

美國財政部10月8日重開29年10個月國債，發售額US$22bn：

• 最高中標收益率：5.618%，較9月高31點子，為2000年8月以來最高
• Bid-to-cover：2.54倍
• 間接投標者獲配：72.3%
• 直接投標者：20.9%
• 一級交易商承接：6.8%
今次中標收益率只較發行前when-issued水平高約0.1點子，定價貼近市場。Bid-to-cover及間接投標比例仍高於近期平均，但弱過9月同類拍賣；一級交易商承接比例亦由9月嘅2.2%回升至6.8%。
MARKET INTERPRETATION
拍賣並非失敗，但亦不宜形容為需求異常強勁。較準確嘅講法係：接近5.6厘嘅收益率仍然吸引到正常至穩健需求。
OUR ANALYSIS

真正訊號唔係「冇人買美債」，而係資金要接近二十六年高位嘅回報，先願意承擔長期利率及通脹風險。

對AI基建、數據中心及其他高capex項目而言，無風險長債已提供超過5%回報，項目嘅現金收益率、殘值與信用保障就必須更有說服力。

【加拿大就業｜兩個月減少約110,000個職位】

加拿大9月就業：

• 就業人數減少68,000，按月跌0.3%
• 就業率由60.8%降至60.6%
• 失業率由6.4%升至6.5%
• 勞動參與率下降0.2個百分點至64.8%
• 8月及9月合計減少約110,000個職位

Reuters調查原先預期增加約9,200個職位，失業率升至6.5%。即係失業率符合預期，但就業人數遠差過市場估算。

跌幅主要集中於：

• 公營部門減少約70,000人
• 私營部門增加約24,000人
• 自僱人士減少約22,500人
• 15至24歲青年減少48,000人
• 25至54歲女性減少28,000人

教育及醫療相關職位合共減少約58,400人。4月至7月曾累計增加約181,000個職位，最近兩個月已回吐約六成。
【加拿大—美國關稅追蹤】

9月係美國新一輪50%關稅生效後首個完整就業月份，但Reuters指出，面向美國市場嘅行業並冇出現顯著高於其他行業嘅職位跌幅。

LFS參考周為9月13日至19日，已涵蓋美國8月22日措施及加拿大9月8日反制關稅；但美國9月29日入口禁令尚未生效。

所以不能將68,000個職位全部定性為「關稅造成」。今次跌幅亦受到公營職位、青年就業、人口與參與率變化等因素影響。

要建立關稅因果鏈，仍要繼續核對：
• 直接受影響行業嘅職位與工時
• 對美出口量、訂單及存貨
• 臨時裁員、就業保險及Work-Sharing使用量
• 多個月份而非單月嘅累積變化
今日未見加拿大或美國公布新增已生效嘅雙邊關稅、豁免或反制措施。

【能源｜風險溢價回落，但供應壓力未解除】

截至約上午7時20分美東時間，近月Brent期油跌逾1%，報每桶略低於US$103。

特朗普稱，美國同伊朗正進行「具成效」嘅討論，並表示11月3日中期選舉前不會恢復軍事攻擊；但佢冇交代參與者、談判框架或正式協議內容。

同日，美國宣布制裁涉及運送伊朗原油、石油產品及石化產品嘅網絡與17艘船隻，對伊朗港口嘅封鎖亦仍然維持。

美國墨西哥灣方面，受颶風Isaias影響，生產商截至星期四已關閉約每日1.3m桶原油產量，相當於當地現有產量約62.9%。

OUR ANALYSIS

今日油價回落主要反映短期地緣風險溢價下降，唔代表供應問題已經解決。

風災停產、霍爾木茲航運、伊朗封鎖及新增制裁仍然存在。真正觀察點係風災後復產速度、航運量，以及美伊會否形成具體協議文本。

【AI融資｜每週監察】

AI Bubble Early-Warning Dashboard本週維持🟠 Orange／Elevated。
REPORTED / UNCONFIRMED INFORMATION
Reuters引述消息人士報道，OpenAI 9月底年度化收入run-rate接近US$50bn，年初約US$20bn，2024年約US$6bn。
早前約US$70bn嘅比較數字，主要來自投資者嘗試用接近Anthropic嘅口徑估算。Anthropic將經AWS及Google Cloud等合作夥伴銷售嘅收入計入總額；OpenAI主要數字則不包括相關合作夥伴銷售。

所以今次差異主要係計算口徑與可比性問題，唔應簡化成OpenAI突然「改口」。不過，年度化run-rate始終唔等於經審計全年收入、盈利或自由現金流。

Firmus方面，公司取消原定約US$5bn澳洲上市計劃，改為尋求私人融資：

• 原定A$11招股價對應股權估值約US$30.6bn，即約A$44bn
• 8月融資估值約US$10.5bn
• 承銷商分析員估計債務約US$30bn
• 企業價值約US$60bn
• 公司目前只有兩個已投入運作嘅租用數據中心
• Reuters引述消息指，CDC Data Centres行政總裁表示雙方原定發展1.6GW AI factories嘅計劃已不再推進

投資者亦關注估值短期急升、債務規模、建設紀錄及交付風險。美國上市晶片股其後下跌3.4%，反映市場對AI投資回報嘅敏感度提高。

WEEKLY ASSESSMENT

需求端仍然強，但收入數據嘅可比性需要加註；融資端則出現更明顯嘅選擇性。

Firmus撤回上市並不足以證明整體AI周期斷裂。較準確嘅結論係：公開市場不再願意無條件接受依賴完美執行、遠期收入及高估值嘅項目。
